U.S. Higher Education.heading: U.S. Higher Education (“USHE”) Segment
U.S. Higher Education.text:
• The USHE segment provides flexible and affordable certificate and degree programs to working adults primarily through Capella University and Strayer University, including the Jack Welch Management Institute MBA, which is an offering of Strayer University. USHE also operates non-degree web and mobile application development courses through Hackbright Academy and Devmountain, which are offerings of Strayer University.

• Capella University is accredited by the Higher Learning Commission and Strayer University is accredited by the Middle States Commission on Higher Education, both higher education institutional accrediting agencies recognized by the U.S. Department of Education. The USHE segment provides academic offerings both online and in physical classrooms, helping working adult students develop specific competencies they can apply in their workplace.

• In the second quarter of 2026, USHE enrollment decreased 0.5% to 85,894 compared to 86,339 for the same period in 2025.

• Trailing 4-quarter student persistence within USHE was 89.0% in the first quarter of 2026 compared to 87.4% for the same period in 2025. Student persistence is calculated as the rate of students continuing from one quarter to the next, adjusted for graduates, on a trailing 4-quarter basis. Student persistence is reported one quarter in arrears.

Education Technology Services.heading: Education Technology Services (“ETS”) Segment
Education Technology Services.text:
• Our ETS segment primarily develops and maintains relationships with employers to build education benefits programs that provide employees access to affordable and industry-relevant training, certificate, and degree programs. The employer relationships developed by the ETS segment are an important source of student enrollment for Capella University and Strayer University, and a significant portion of the revenue attributed to the ETS segment is driven by the volume of enrollment derived from these employer relationships. Enrollments attributed to the ETS segment are determined based on a student’s employment status and the existence of a corporate partnership arrangement with SEI. All enrollments attributed to the ETS segment continue to be attributed to the segment until the student graduates or withdraws, even if his or her employment status changes or if the partnership contract expires.

• In the second quarter of 2026, employer affiliated enrollment as a percentage of USHE enrollment was 34.7% compared to 31.8% for the same period in 2025.

• ETS also supports employer partners through Workforce Edge, a platform which provides employers a full-service education benefits administration solution, and Sophia Learning, which offers low-cost online general education-level courses recommended by the American Council on Education for credit at other colleges and universities.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Short-term investments
lines.why: Securities held for the cash they will return: financial.

lines.name: Long-term investments
lines.why: Securities held for their return: financial. A stake in another business that is part of operations is operating.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Equity-method investments
lines.why: Stakes in associated businesses, usually part of operations. Financial if held as an investment.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue, non-current
lines.why: Customers' payments for later years: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.
